findings.claim: Carrier tiers are derived with an unknown size (classify(carrier_sha, None) in own/classify.py, carriers loop), so every carrier that is not in Git or an archive is labelled DRIVE_ONLY_DBX_UNKNOWN_OVER_4MIB regardless of its real size; 34 of the 43 carriers so labelled are 4 MiB or less and their Dropbox identity is derivable.
findings.evidence: Joining each carrier id to its snapshot record gives sizes for all 43 UNKNOWN carriers; 34 are <= 4,194,304 bytes (5,558 to 3,511,071 bytes). Re-deriving content_hash = sha256(sha256) for those 34: 32 are absent from the Dropbox table (true tier DRIVE_ONLY) and 2 are present (true tier DBX_EXACT; carrier sizes 131,069 and 2,561,890 bytes). The snapshot records already carry these correct tiers for the same ids, so the publication is internally inconsistent. Affected outputs: carrier_tier column for 34 of 73 rows in ARCHIVE_CARRIERS.tsv; SUMMARY.json archive_members.carriers_by_tier (43/29/1 should be DRIVE_ONLY 32, GIT_EXACT 29, DRIVE_ONLY_DBX_UNKNOWN_OVER_4MIB 9, DBX_EXACT 2, ARCHIVE_EXACT 1); README 'Carriers by tier' line; and the README sentence '3,267 are found nowhere else (all inside carriers over 4 MiB whose Dropbox identity is not derivable)' is false: 2,530 of the 3,267 NOT_FOUND members sit in carriers of 4 MiB or less whose Dropbox identity is derivable and absent, only 737 sit in carriers over 4 MiB. The MEMBER/VIA_CARRIER/NOT_FOUND counts themselves do not change (the 44 members of the two DBX_EXACT carriers are already MEMBER).
findings.fix: In classify.py pass the carrier's snapshot byte count (lookup by carrier id in the per-item records) to classify() instead of None, rebuild carriers, ARCHIVE_CARRIERS.tsv, SUMMARY.json and README; reword the NOT_FOUND sentence to split carriers over 4 MiB (identity not derivable) from carriers of 4 MiB or less (derivable, not in Dropbox).

findings.claim: derive_ch (content_hash = sha256(sha256(bytes))) is not the Dropbox rule for empty files, whose content_hash is sha256 of the empty string; the README states the rule without this carve-out.

findings.claim: The Liveness bullet and paragraph say the listing 'marks snapshot items touched since the snapshot' and that STALE_SAME_SIZE 'means touched after the snapshot with the same byte count (moves and renames bump the time)'; the published counts CHANGED_AFTER_SNAPSHOT 349 and STALE_SAME_SIZE 277 (also in SUMMARY.json liveness.*) therefore over-state change since the snapshot.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from the ten live-listing TSVs: the listing cutoff is 2026-09-17T00:00Z, i.e. the start of the snapshot day, not the snapshot time (the inventory records carry no modifiedTime, so the scripts cannot compare). 266 of the 349 CHANGED files have createdTime == modifiedTime in the connector's own metadata (245 dated 2026-09-17, 18 dated 09-18, 3 dated 09-19) - they were never modified after creation, yet they are in the snapshot publication, so the snapshot saw their final state. 234 of the 277 STALE_SAME_SIZE digests belong to such files, and all 234 have the same title and the same parent folder as in the snapshot, so 'moves and renames' does not explain them. Only 64 CHANGED files (35 STALE_SAME_SIZE) have a live modifiedTime on or after 2026-09-18. The direction is conservative for digests (more marked stale than warranted) but the sentences are false as statements of fact.
findings.fix: Either (a) rename the status to what the listing shows (MODIFIED_AFTER_2026-09-17T00Z) and state that the cutoff pre-dates the snapshot time, or (b) treat items with createdTime == modifiedTime as untouched (digest CURRENT) and report 349 -> 83 possibly-changed files and 277 -> 43 possibly-stale digests, giving both numbers; in either case drop the '(moves and renames bump the time)' explanation or support it with a title/parent comparison.

findings.claim: 'a digest is CURRENT only for untouched items' (Liveness bullet) and 'nothing modified after the snapshot has a current digest here' (Limits) do not describe the published data.
findings.evidence: 26 hashed files have live_status CHANGED_AFTER_SNAPSHOT and digest_state CURRENT (23 from the 2026-09-18 delta, 3 from 2026-09-19): liveness.py marks a digest CURRENT when a dated delta re-hashed the item at or after the live modifiedTime. CURRENT 1,799 therefore includes 26 touched items with a valid later digest.
findings.fix: State the actual rule: CURRENT = not in the listing, or re-hashed by a dated delta (18-20 September) at or after the item's last modification; amend the Limits bullet to 'nothing modified after the last delta (2026-09-20) has a current digest here'.
